newsitem.title: GERMANY: Heavy rain may cause some lodging in German grain.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain may cause some lodging in German grain.

text.p: German grain crops may suffer some quality losses from lodging, when grain bends over and breaks, after recent heavy rains, an official at the DWD national meteorological office said.
But Germany should still harvest another record crop this year as its grain regions have not suffered the flood damage seen in neighbouring east European countries.
"Some south-eastern German states and some regions in Bavaria recorded heavy rainfall totalling 100 litres per square metre over the last week," the DWD source said.
"This means grain becomes difficult to harvest and farmers will incur drying costs."
DWD said rain over Germany should ease this week but there could be more showers from the weekend onwards.
The most grain-intensive regions in the North, Schleswig Holstein and Lower Saxony, had not been affected by the heavy rain.
The ZMP farm price office in Bonn was therefore optimistic for the harvest.
"Eastern Germany has now started harvesting and it looks as if there will be another record crop," a ZMP official said.
"Yields and qualities vary but there is no need to assume serious losses or damage."
Heavy rain supplied light soils in eastern Germany with welcome moisture.
Grain trader Toepfer on Friday said the German grain crop may exceed 19997's record 42.1 million tonnes by 900,000 tonnes.
